mean: wherever you live, you come to like it once you settle in
lit: live there, and it becomes the capital: any place feels like the finest city once it is home

use.how: A complete remark, or followed by で or というもの, about a place that seemed unappealing at first but became home: 最初は不安だったけど、住めば都だ。

near.t: 郷に入っては郷に従え
near.diff: 郷に入っては郷に従え is advice to follow local customs; 住めば都 says you grow fond of a place once you live there.

cue: You dreaded moving to a small town with one shop and no cinema, but two years later you would hate to leave.

ctx.en: The house is far from the station, but you get used to anywhere, and now I really like it.

ctx.en: "Isn't it lonely since you moved to the country?" "At first, yes. But wherever you live becomes home."

ctx.s: {住[す]めば都[みやこ]}と言[い]うから、あまり心配[しんぱい]しないで新[あたら]しい町[まち]に行[い]っておいで。
ctx.en: They say anywhere feels like home once you live there, so don't worry too much and off you go to your new town.

ctx.en: My brother, who did nothing but complain about his cramped dorm, was sad to leave it when he graduated. You come to love wherever you live.

ctx.s: 海外赴任[かいがいふにん]が決[き]まった時[とき]は不安[ふあん]だったが、{住[す]めば都[みやこ]}、三年[さんねん]で第二[だいに]の故郷[こきょう]になった。
ctx.en: I was anxious when I was posted abroad, but you settle in anywhere, and in three years it became my second home.

ctx.s: 不便[ふべん]な島[しま]の暮[く]らしも{住[す]めば都[みやこ]}というもので、今[いま]では都会[とかい]に戻[もど]りたいとは思[おも]わない。
ctx.en: Even inconvenient island life becomes home once you live it, and now I have no wish to go back to the city.

bad.en: (meant: the hotel we stayed at for one night was very comfortable)
bad.why: It is about growing fond of a place by living there over time. A one-night stay, or a place that was good from the start, does not fit.

bad.en: (meant: Tokyo is the capital of Japan)

mean: for any job, it is best to leave it to the specialist
lit: for rice cakes, go to the rice-cake maker

use.how: A complete remark, often after やっぱり, when a professional does far better than an amateur, or as advice to hand a job to one: やっぱり餅は餅屋だね。
